winner.text: Replace the raw 24-category hour feature with a train-fitted six-bin four-hour categorical feature.
winner.rationale: Hour-specific diagnostics are weak across many adjacent hours, which may indicate that the current 24-way hour effect is too granular for stable temporal transfer. Coarsening is a single representation ablation using only request-time information. Downside: it can erase real hour-level preference variation and lower top-five precision.
winner.exact_ablation: Replace only the existing hour categorical field with floor(hour/4), yielding six train-fitted hour-bin categories and an unknown bucket; retain user_id, video_id, tab, weekday, additive architecture, K=4 uniform sampling, pairwise loss, optimizer, regularization, and all other settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Change by -0.0003 to 0.0009 because pooling adjacent hours can reduce variance while sacrificing detail.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Change by -0.0003 to 0.0011 if more stable time effects improve top-five ordering.

selection_rationale: Select c11. It is the consultant's top-ranked option (utility 0.63) and offers the best reliability-adjusted path: a single, low-risk simplification of the already validated request-context feature family. Broad weakness across adjacent, high-volume hour slices supports reducing variance in the current 24-category hour effect, while avoiding the sparsity and exposure-pattern overfitting risks of high-cardinality video-context interactions. Its expected primary gain is positive (0.0004), confidence is moderate (4), and runtime and leakage risks are low; it also preserves experiment 4's strongest confirmed pairwise-ranking configuration.
